site.name: booking
site.summary: booking-clone Clone of the Booking.com hotel booking funnel (home → city list → area filters → detail → room → booking → confirmation), plus other business-line and supporting pages. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Home: search bar (destination / check-in & out dates / guests), recommended destinations, recent searches, Genius membership prompt, business-line entries in the footer | | `tokyo.html` | Tokyo hotel list: left filter panel (price, stars, rating, amenities, area), right-hand hotel cards (price, rating, review count, distance, free-cancellation tag), sort bar, map entry | | `shinjuku.html` | Shinjuku-area hotel list, same structure as above, pre-filtered to Shinjuku |

run_plan.goal: Explore and critique the Booking.com-style booking experience end to end, with deepest coverage on the hotel booking funnel from home/search through confirmation, while also sampling adjacent travel products, account/support pages, and post-booking management states on desktop and mobile.
run_plan.summary: Start by validating the primary hotel funnel that the prescan clearly exposes: index.html → tokyo/shinjuku results → hotel detail → room selection → reservation → confirmation. Then expand into nearby decision and recovery paths such as reviews, my trips, help, sign-in/register, and the secondary business lines surfaced in the global nav. Because several pages show dense filters, many small tap targets, and some missing input labels, prioritize interaction clarity, state persistence, and mobile usability on search/listing and booking form pages.
assumptions: The main hotel flow is statically linked and should be traversable via visible links/buttons rather than a true backend search submission.
Tokyo/Shinjuku pages represent the intended listing/filter experience for the primary accommodation funnel.
Confirmation, my-trips, and support pages are available as post-booking and recovery states rather than requiring authenticated backend data.
Secondary flows available for exploration are limited to the pages seen in prescan: flights, car rentals, attractions, airport taxis, deals, list-property, help, sign-in, and register.
risk_hotspots: index.html search bar inputs and Search CTA: core entry point, visible as inputs without a form, needs validation of affordance and routing
tokyo.html filter panel and sort controls: very high control density with 35 inputs and a visible 'No properties match your filters' state worth provoking/checking
shinjuku.html pre-filtered results and empty-state behavior: confirm area-specific filtering, card quality, and reset/discoverability
hotel-detail.html availability/reserve area: critical bridge from browsing to booking, needs pricing/date consistency and CTA clarity
hotel-detail-granbell.html reserve path: secondary property comparison path to ensure alternate hotel pages behave consistently
reviews.html sort dropdown and traveler-type tabs: check content filtering, state changes, and readability of social proof
room-selection.html price summary and onward CTA: verify selected room, taxes, cancellation, and 'Continue to booking details' continuity
reservation.html guest details form: 12 inputs, radio choices, special requests, arrival time/payment/cancellation messaging, and at least one missing input label
confirmation.html booking summary and next-step links: verify final-state completeness, reassurance, and cross-sell intrusiveness
my-trips.html tabs and action buttons like Cancel booking / Modify dates / Write a review / Book again: post-booking management and recovery affordances
flights.html trip-type radios, cabin-class select, and search/results relationship: multi-control search UI complexity
car-rentals.html 'Drop car off at different location' control and search/result cards: checkbox/toggle clarity plus deal CTA flow
airport-taxis.html unlabeled inputs and repeated Book CTAs: transport-booking clarity and transfer option comparison
help.html search plus topic cards and chat/call actions: support discoverability and escalation paths
signin.html and register.html account-entry forms: form clarity, password expectations, alternate sign-in buttons, and low-friction routing
Mobile nav/header controls across pages: prescan already shows many small tap targets in top navigation and footer/support links

phases.title: Primary hotel discovery and search entry
phases.objective: Validate how a user starts a stay search from the homepage and reaches browseable hotel results, including alternative discovery links.
key_checks: Use the home search inputs as presented and activate Search to confirm expected routing into results
Compare entry via homepage Search versus Tokyo destination cards/links to see whether the same results context is reached
Inspect search-field defaults and whether destination/date/guest context is visible and understandable on results pages
Exercise at least several Tokyo/Shinjuku filters and a sort option to check discoverability, feedback, and whether results/empty-state messaging stays coherent
If possible, trigger or inspect the visible 'No properties match your filters' state and assess recoverability/reset options
Check map entry visibility and usefulness as surfaced in the list pages
exit_criteria: A repeatable path from index.html to hotel results is confirmed
At least one listing page filter interaction and one sort interaction have been exercised
Evidence is gathered on whether search context and result counts remain understandable after changes

phases.title: Property evaluation and selection
phases.objective: Assess how effectively listing pages support comparison and how hotel detail/reviews pages help users decide before booking.
key_checks: Open at least two property details from results, including Park Hyatt Tokyo and Shinjuku Granbell Hotel, to compare consistency of layout and CTA prominence
Validate breadcrumb/back-to-results behavior and whether users can easily return to browsing without losing context
Check that core decision info is easy to find: location score, review count, facilities, highlights, pricing for 3 nights, and availability area
Enter or inspect guest reviews from the property flow and exercise review sorting and traveler-type filters
Look for mismatches between listing-card promises and property-detail specifics such as free cancellation, breakfast, and pricing framing
exit_criteria: Two hotel detail pages have been inspected and compared
At least one route into reviews.html has been exercised
Booking-decision information hierarchy and any inconsistencies between list/detail/reviews have been documented

phases.title: Checkout and confirmation funnel
phases.objective: Walk the main reservation funnel end to end and validate continuity, clarity, and trust signals from room choice through confirmation.
key_checks: Use the property reserve/availability path to enter room-selection.html and confirm room/date/guest details carry forward
Validate price summary structure across room selection, reservation, and confirmation, including taxes, city tax, cancellation timing, and payment timing
Complete reservation form interactions using visible fields: first name, last name, email, country/region, phone, booking-for-self/other, and special requests
Check required-field signaling, label clarity, placeholder dependence, and whether form sections like arrival time/payment schedule/cancellation are understandable
Proceed to confirmation and verify booking reference, property details, dates, room details, and reassurance content are complete and internally consistent
Assess whether cross-sell links on confirmation support the user without overwhelming the completed-booking state
exit_criteria: A full path from hotel detail to confirmation is completed
Continuity of selected room, price, and policy information across all checkout pages is verified
At least one form-quality issue or success pattern is captured from reservation.html

phases.title: Post-booking management, support, and account access
phases.objective: Test adjacent flows users rely on after or around booking: trip management, support, sign-in, and registration.
key_checks: From confirmation and/or global/footer nav, enter my-trips.html and test tabs such as Upcoming, Completed, and Cancelled
Exercise visible trip actions including View details, Cancel booking, Modify dates, Write a review, and Book again where available
Use help.html search and topic tiles to assess findability of cancellation, payment/refund, change-booking, and account/security help
Inspect chat and call CTAs for prominence and expected behavior
Review sign-in and registration flows for input clarity, password expectations, alternate auth options, and smooth cross-linking between sign in and create account
exit_criteria: Trip-management and support pages have each had multiple visible controls exercised
At least one recovery-oriented path is validated from booking/confirmation into support or management
Sign-in and register pages are both inspected for UX blockers and consistency

phases.title: Secondary product lines and mobile verification
phases.objective: Sample the non-hotel business lines linked in global navigation and repeat critical checks on mobile for responsiveness and tap usability.
key_checks: Visit each secondary product page from the nav or direct route and exercise its main search/filter CTA at least once
In flights.html, switch among trip types and inspect cabin-class select plus results-to-selection affordance
In car-rentals.html, toggle 'Drop car off at different location' and inspect deal-card progression
In attractions.html and airport-taxis.html, compare search clarity, card content, and booking CTA prominence
Inspect deals.html and list-property.html as promotional/partner-entry experiences for relevance and navigation quality

On mobile viewport, repeat the critical hotel flow checkpoints on index, results, hotel detail, reservation, and my-trips, focusing on header nav, tap-target size, filter usability, and form completion
exit_criteria: All secondary-nav pages discovered in prescan have been visited and at least lightly exercised
Critical mobile checks are completed on the main hotel path plus one post-booking page
Responsive issues and small-tap-target impacts are documented with concrete examples

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 19 known HTML pages, with deepest interaction coverage on index.html, tokyo.html, shinjuku.html, hotel-detail.html, room-selection.html, reservation.html, confirmation.html, my-trips.html, and help.html.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise most visible controls on key pages: homepage search, listing filters/sort/map entry, property reserve/reviews links, room-selection onward CTA, reservation form fields/radios/textarea, confirmation next steps, my-trips tabs/actions, help search/topics, sign-in/register forms, and the primary search/booking controls on each secondary product page.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical checks on mobile viewport for the main hotel funnel (index → results → hotel detail → reservation → confirmation) plus my-trips and one secondary product page, with emphasis on navigation collapse/clarity, tap target adequacy, dense filter interaction, and form readability.

notes: Do not spend disproportionate time on placeholder links with href '#'; prefer pages and controls with real navigable destinations seen in the prescan.

Prescan shows repeated small tap-target warnings across nav/footer plus missing input labels on airport-taxis.html, attractions.html, car-rentals.html, reservation.html, tokyo.html, and shinjuku.html; treat these as likely recurring usability themes to verify rather than assume.
Because there are no prescan-reported console or network errors, prioritize UX flow quality, consistency, and responsiveness over technical fault hunting.

ux_notes: Clicking the homepage 'Search' CTA successfully routes to the hotel results page (`tokyo.html`), matching the expected next step in the booking funnel.

The results page preserves key search context in the top search bar: destination ('Tokyo, Japan'), dates ('Tue, Jul 15 — Fri, Jul 18'), and party size ('2 adults · 0 children · 1 room'), which supports clarity about what the search returned.
Results immediately reinforce the search outcome with a prominent heading ('Tokyo: 6,842 properties found') and visible hotel cards, reducing ambiguity after the CTA.

A concrete UX issue is present on the results page search form: the destination input has no label/aria-label/placeholder per the DOM/layout warning, which weakens accessibility despite the visible filled value.

observation.title: Park Hyatt Tokyo - Booking.com
observation.visible_text: Booking.com Stays Flights Car rentals Attractions Airport taxis JPY List your property Sign in Home > Japan > Tokyo > Shinjuku > Park Hyatt Tokyo ← Back to results ★★★★★ Park Hyatt Tokyo 📍 3-7-1-2 Nishi Shinjuku, Shinjuku, Tokyo, 163-1055, Japan · Excellent location — rated 9.6/10 🏯 🛌 🍵 🏊 🌄 About Park Hyatt Tokyo Occupying the top 14 floors of the 52-story Shinjuku Park Tower, Park Hyatt Tokyo offers panoramic views of the city skyline and Mount Fuji. The hotel features the renowned New York Grill restaurant, a 20-meter indoor swimming pool, and the Club on the Park fitness center with a stunning view of the city. Each room is spacious and elegantly designed with floor-to-ceiling windows, deep soaking tubs, and original artwork. observation.title: Park Hyatt Tokyo - Guest Reviews - Booking.com
observation.visible_text: Booking.com Stays Flights Car rentals Attractions JPY Sign in Home > Tokyo > Park Hyatt Tokyo > Guest reviews Guest reviews Park Hyatt Tokyo 9.4 Exceptional 3,847 reviews Staff 9.6 Facilities 9.4 Cleanliness 9.6 Comfort 9.5 Value for money 8.8 Location 9.6 Free WiFi 9.2 Breakfast 9.3 All reviews (3,847) Most relevant Most recent Highest score Lowest score All Couples (1,234) Families (876) Solo travellers (543) Business (1,194) TK Takeshi Japan · Couple · Deluxe King Room · 3 nights 10 Absolutely perfect in every way 👍 Liked The views from the 47th floor were breathtaking. Staff remembered our names from the first interaction. The New York Grill breakfast is worth every yen. Pool area is serene and never crowded. 👎 Disliked Nothing to complain about. Perhaps the walk from Shinjuku station is a bit long in summer heat, but the hotel shuttle solves that. Reviewed: June 2025 SM Sarah M. United States · Solo traveller · Park King Room · 5 nights 9.6 Lost in Translation vibes, but better 👍 Liked The atmosphere is exactly what you'd hope for. The library lounge is perfect for quiet afternoons. Girandole breakfast buffet has incredible variety. The bed is the most comfortable I've ever slept in. 👎 Disliked Price is steep, but you get what you pay for. The gym can get busy in the early morning. Reviewed: May 2025 LW Li Wei China · Family · Deluxe Twin Room · 4 nights 9.2 Excellent for families with older children 👍 Liked Spacious rooms, impeccable service. The concierge helped us plan our entire Tokyo itinerary. Kids loved the pool. Location is quiet but still accessible to everything. 👎 Disliked Not many kid-specific amenities. The restaurant dress code made dinner with teenagers a bit formal. Would appreciate a kids' menu. Reviewed: April 2025 JB James B. United Kingdom · Business · Park Suite · 2 nights 9.8 The gold standard for business travel 👍 Liked The suite is extraordinary — separate living area, stunning views, and the bathroom alone is larger than most Tokyo hotel rooms. Club lounge access made early mornings productive. Flawless check-in process. 👎 Disliked Honestly nothing. If I had to nitpick, the in-room coffee machine could be upgraded to a proper espresso machine at this price point. Reviewed: March 2025 YK Yuki K. Japan · Couple · Deluxe King Room · 1 night 8.8 Anniversary celebration done right 👍 Liked They arranged a beautiful cake and champagne for our anniversary without us asking — the concierge noticed it in our booking notes. The Peak Bar at sunset is magical. 👎 Disliked For a one-night stay, the value proposition is harder to justify. The minibar prices are quite high even by luxury hotel standards. ux_notes: The click achieved the objective by opening attractions.html with an above-the-fold discovery module: a destination field, date field, and prominent blue Search button under the heading “Attractions, activities and experiences.”

The page supports quick scanning with two content tiers: simple top-attraction cards showing area, star rating/review count, and price/free-entry status, followed by richer “Experiences & tours” cards that add category, duration, description, per-person pricing, and visible “Book now” CTAs.

Booking CTA prominence is mixed: only the tour cards expose explicit “Book now” buttons, while the top-attraction cards show price/free-entry but no visible CTA, creating weaker action clarity for those items.

Trust and decision support are strong on visible cards because they include review volume and ratings (for example “4.8 (2,345 reviews)” and star counts like “(12,456)”), plus concrete pricing such as “From JPY 8,500 per person.”

There is an accessibility clarity issue in the search controls: the date input has a layout warning for missing label/aria-label/placeholder, even though it visually shows “Jul 15 — Jul 18,” which may reduce screen-reader clarity.

ux_notes: The click achieved the objective by opening deals.html, where promotions are clearly structured with recognizable sections like 'Unlock Genius discounts worldwide,' 'Limited-time offers in Japan,' 'Summer travel deals,' and 'Flight + Hotel packages.'

Offer cards present trust-building specifics such as original vs discounted nightly prices, percentage-off badges, ratings, neighborhoods, and explicit validity dates (for example 'Valid until Aug 31, 2025'), making the promotions easier to evaluate.

Promotions are connected back into booking flows through direct links like 'View deal' to hotel-detail.html and 'Find deals'/'Explore early deals' to tokyo.html, so the page supports onward shopping rather than acting as a dead-end.

Several primary nav and CTA elements are flagged with low-severity small tap target warnings (for example Stays 69x39, Sign in 77x37, View deal 309x32/37), indicating weaker mobile ergonomics even though the desktop page is usable.

Footer support/discover links such as 'Manage your trips', 'Contact Customer Service', 'Genius loyalty program', and others still point to '#', which weakens the credibility and navigation completeness of a promotions page.

ux_notes: The airport taxis page opened successfully and exposes the full booking flow at a glance: four trip inputs, a prominent Search CTA, and multiple transfer cards with repeated Book CTAs.

Two trip fields are accessibility-unclear: the date/time input (ux-11) and passenger input (ux-12) have no label, aria-label, or placeholder per layout warnings, which makes those controls harder to interpret for assistive tech.

CTA hierarchy is potentially repetitive: after the top-level Search button, each transfer option repeats the same generic 'Book' CTA, so users may need to rely on surrounding card text to distinguish what they are booking.

The page provides reassuring purchase signals directly on each card—fixed price, free cancellation, meet & greet, journey estimate—and a separate 'Why book your airport taxi with us?' section, which supports decision confidence.

observation.title: Park Hyatt Tokyo - Booking.com
observation.visible_text: Booking.com Stays Flights Car rentals Attractions Airport taxis JPY List your property Sign in Home > Japan > Tokyo > Shinjuku > Park Hyatt Tokyo ← Back to results ★★★★★ Park Hyatt Tokyo 📍 3-7-1-2 Nishi Shinjuku, Shinjuku, Tokyo, 163-1055, Japan · Excellent location — rated 9.6/10 🏯 🛌 🍵 🏊 🌄 About Park Hyatt Tokyo Occupying the top 14 floors of the 52-story Shinjuku Park Tower, Park Hyatt Tokyo offers panoramic views of the city skyline and Mount Fuji. The hotel features the renowned New York Grill restaurant, a 20-meter indoor swimming pool, and the Club on the Park fitness center with a stunning view of the city. Each room is spacious and elegantly designed with floor-to-ceiling windows, deep soaking tubs, and original artwork. The hotel is located in the Nishi-Shinjuku business district, a 12-minute walk from Shinjuku Station. Guests can enjoy the Girandole restaurant for all-day dining, the Peak Bar for cocktails with a view, and the Kozue restaurant for authentic Japanese cuisine. The spa offers a range of treatments in a serene setting on the 45th floor. observation.title: Park Hyatt Tokyo - Guest Reviews - Booking.com
observation.visible_text: Booking.com Stays Flights Car rentals Attractions JPY Sign in Home > Tokyo > Park Hyatt Tokyo > Guest reviews Guest reviews Park Hyatt Tokyo 9.4 Exceptional 3,847 reviews Staff 9.6 Facilities 9.4 Cleanliness 9.6 Comfort 9.5 Value for money 8.8 Location 9.6 Free WiFi 9.2 Breakfast 9.3 All reviews (3,847) Most relevant Most recent Highest score Lowest score All Couples (1,234) Families (876) Solo travellers (543) Business (1,194) TK Takeshi Japan · Couple · Deluxe King Room · 3 nights 10 Absolutely perfect in every way 👍 Liked The views from the 47th floor were breathtaking. Staff remembered our names from the first interaction. The New York Grill breakfast is worth every yen. Pool area is serene and never crowded. 👎 Disliked Nothing to complain about. Perhaps the walk from Shinjuku station is a bit long in summer heat, but the hotel shuttle solves that. Reviewed: June 2025 SM Sarah M. United States · Solo traveller · Park King Room · 5 nights 9.6 Lost in Translation vibes, but better 👍 Liked The atmosphere is exactly what you'd hope for. The library lounge is perfect for quiet afternoons. Girandole breakfast buffet has incredible variety. The bed is the most comfortable I've ever slept in. 👎 Disliked Price is steep, but you get what you pay for. The gym can get busy in the early morning. Reviewed: May 2025 LW Li Wei China · Family · Deluxe Twin Room · 4 nights 9.2 Excellent for families with older children 👍 Liked Spacious rooms, impeccable service. The concierge helped us plan our entire Tokyo itinerary. Kids loved the pool. Location is quiet but still accessible to everything. 👎 Disliked Not many kid-specific amenities. The restaurant dress code made dinner with teenagers a bit formal. Would appreciate a kids' menu. Reviewed: April 2025 JB James B. United Kingdom · Business · Park Suite · 2 nights 9.8 The gold standard for business travel 👍 Liked The suite is extraordinary — separate living area, stunning views, and the bathroom alone is larger than most Tokyo hotel rooms. Club lounge access made early mornings productive. Flawless check-in process. 👎 Disliked Honestly nothing. If I had to nitpick, the in-room coffee machine could be upgraded to a proper espresso machine at this price point. Reviewed: March 2025 YK Yuki K. Japan · Couple · Deluxe King Room · 1 night 8.8 Anniversary celebration done right 👍 Liked They arranged a beautiful cake and champagne for our anniversary without us asking — the concierge noticed it in our booking notes. The Peak Bar at sunset is magical. 👎 Disliked For a one-night stay, the value proposition is harder to justify. The minibar prices are quite high even by luxury hotel standards. Staff remembered our names from the first interaction. The New York Grill breakfast is worth every yen. Pool area is serene and never crowded. 👎 Disliked Nothing to complain about. Perhaps the walk from Shinjuku station is a bit long in summer heat, but the hotel shuttle solves that. Reviewed: June 2025 SM Sarah M. United States · Solo traveller · Park King Room · 5 nights 9.6 Lost in Translation vibes, but better 👍 Liked The atmosphere is exactly what you'd hope for. The library lounge is perfect for quiet afternoons. Girandole breakfast buffet has incredible variety. The bed is the most comfortable I've ever slept in. 👎 Disliked Price is steep, but you get what you pay for. The gym can get busy in the early morning. Reviewed: May 2025 LW Li Wei China · Family · Deluxe Twin Room · 4 nights 9.2 Excellent for families with older children 👍 Liked Spacious rooms, impeccable service. The concierge helped us plan our entire Tokyo itinerary. Kids loved the pool. Location is quiet but still accessible to everything. 👎 Disliked Not many kid-specific amenities. The restaurant dress code made dinner with teenagers a bit formal. Would appreciate a kids' menu. Reviewed: April 2025 JB James B. ux_notes: The second budget checkbox was successfully added: both 'JPY 20,000 - 40,000' and 'JPY 40,000 - 80,000' now appear as selected chips with dismiss × controls plus a visible 'Clear all' recovery action.
The page gives coherent narrowing feedback after multi-select by updating the heading to 'Tokyo: 6 properties found' and keeping listings visible under the active price chips.

There is mixed clarity in the filtered results: despite selecting mid/high nightly budget bands, visible cards still show much higher 3-night totals like JPY 198,000 and JPY 245,000, which can make the budget logic hard to understand against the 'per night' filter label.

step.objective: Learn whether the 'Clear all' control provides obvious, trustworthy recovery from a narrowed filter state and restores the broader results context cleanly.
step.success_criteria: Active budget chips disappear, checkboxes reset, and the results count/listings return to a broader Tokyo state without confusing leftover filtered messaging.

result.feedback: Visible content changed after the action.

ux_notes: The action did not test sorting because `select_option` targeted `ux-13`, which is the Search button, and the tool returned `No selectable option found for ux-13.`

The sort UI remains visible as `Our top picks` in the results header, and the top visible hotel prices are still not lowest-first (JPY 198,000, then JPY 245,000, while a later visible listing shows JPY 135,000), which provides no evidence that hotel ordering changed.

observation.title: Park Hyatt Tokyo - Booking.com
observation.visible_text: Booking.com Stays Flights Car rentals Attractions Airport taxis JPY List your property Sign in Home > Japan > Tokyo > Shinjuku > Park Hyatt Tokyo ← Back to results ★★★★★ Park Hyatt Tokyo 📍 3-7-1-2 Nishi Shinjuku, Shinjuku, Tokyo, 163-1055, Japan · Excellent location — rated 9.6/10 🏯 🛌 🍵 🏊 🌄 About Park Hyatt Tokyo Occupying the top 14 floors of the 52-story Shinjuku Park Tower, Park Hyatt Tokyo offers panoramic views of the city skyline and Mount Fuji. The hotel features the renowned New York Grill restaurant, a 20-meter indoor swimming pool, and the Club on the Park fitness center with a stunning view of the city. Each room is spacious and elegantly designed with floor-to-ceiling windows, deep soaking tubs, and original artwork. The hotel is located in the Nishi-Shinjuku business district, a 12-minute walk from Shinjuku Station. Guests can enjoy the Girandole restaurant for all-day dining, the Peak Bar for cocktails with a view, and the Kozue restaurant for authentic Japanese cuisine. The spa offers a range of treatments in a serene setting on the 45th floor. This misfire suggests the large hotel card is a broad clickable area; users trying to interact with nearby comparison controls could be taken into a detail page unexpectedly.

step.objective: Learn whether the detail page’s back-to-results link returns users to the listing context cleanly after an unintended navigation from a broad clickable hotel card.
step.success_criteria: Navigation returns to tokyo.html and preserves understandable listing context, helping assess recovery from accidental deep-linking.

ux_notes: The tiny mobile budget checkbox was still operable: tool feedback confirms ux-17 changed from unchecked to checked despite being only 16x16px and flagged as a small tap target.
Filter feedback is visible after selection: the page shows an active chip 'JPY 0 - 10,000 ×' and the results summary updates to 'Tokyo: 6 properties found,' indicating the filter took effect.

Mobile filter comprehension is weakened by layout breakage: the page has horizontal overflow (813px content width on a 390px viewport), and the screenshot shows the results list pushed off to the right while the filter column remains on the left.
Results messaging appears contradictory: the DOM contains both 'Tokyo: 6 properties found' and the heading 'No properties match your filters' at the same time after the filter is applied.

step.objective: Gather stronger evidence about mobile usability on the Tokyo results page, especially whether the split filter/results layout and off-screen cards hinder browsing and recovery.

observation.title: Shinjuku Granbell Hotel - Booking.com
observation.visible_text: Booking.com Stays Flights Car rentals Attractions Airport taxis JPY List your property Sign in Home > Japan > Tokyo > Shinjuku > Shinjuku Granbell Hotel ★★★ Shinjuku Granbell Hotel 📍 2-14-5 Kabukicho, Shinjuku, Tokyo, 160-0021, Japan · Very Good location — rated 8.4/10 🏙 🛌 🍵 🏊 🌄 About Shinjuku Granbell Hotel Located in the heart of Shinjuku, the Granbell Hotel offers modern accommodations just a 5-minute walk from Shinjuku-Sanchome Station. The hotel features stylish rooms with contemporary Japanese design, a rooftop bar with panoramic city views, and easy access to Tokyo's vibrant nightlife and shopping districts. Each room is thoughtfully designed with comfortable bedding, free WiFi, and modern amenities. The hotel is surrounded by restaurants, convenience stores, and is within walking distance of Kabukicho entertainment district and Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden. Guests can enjoy the on-site restaurant serving Japanese and international cuisine, relax at the rooftop terrace, and explore the many attractions nearby including Meiji Shrine and Takeshita Street in Harajuku.
